# Pre-split cache fixtures

`pre_split_profile.json` is the profile serialized by the pre-split binary.
`pre_split_preparation.json` was captured from production code at commit
`00c1038153d86c2060ed948f57fdc8053c56d643`, using Rust 1.99.0 and the pinned q8
EmbeddingGemma 2 model in the local Hugging Face cache. It is not generated by
the new implementation or reconstructed from copied hash algorithms.

The capture loads real Gemma (128 dimensions, text only), builds `SearchEngine`
with its default segmenter, and calls the engine's private `prepare` method on
three synthetic inputs. The titled Markdown case exercises heading/file title
composition and link-target stripping; the plain-text case has no title; the
image case hashes fixed synthetic bytes without decoding or inference. It also
captures BLAKE3 hashes of little-endian normalized vector bytes at all four
widths, from deterministic integer-valued raw model outputs.

To reproduce in a temporary source tree, from the current worktree:

```sh
split_base=$(mktemp -d)
git archive 00c1038153d86c2060ed948f57fdc8053c56d643 | tar -x -C "$split_base"
cat crates/seyk-core/tests/fixtures/capture_pre_split.rs >> "$split_base/src/engine.rs"
cd "$split_base"
export PATH="$(rustup run 1.99.0 rustc --print sysroot)/bin:$PATH"
rustup run 1.99.0 cargo test --lib --locked capture_pre_split_profile_and_inputs
# Read /tmp/embed-fix-pre-split-golden.json; do not regenerate from current code.
```

Ordinary workspace tests check engine preparation/profile construction using
the frozen model identity and check model-output normalization byte hashes.
`tests/cache_profile_golden.rs::real_gemma_and_engine_match_pre_split_profile`
additionally loads the current real backend and checks its generated identity
and the engine's generated profile together; this test needs local weights and
is ignored in ordinary CI. Core keeps no backend dependency.

The self-made `support/pdf_fixture.rs::malformed_cmap` generator reproduces both
CMap panics seen on real PDFs: an overlapping ToUnicode mapping with an unknown
FontAwesome glyph (`unexpected entry in unicode map`), and a three-byte
bfrange destination (`bad length of hexstring`). No IRPAPERS PDF bytes are used
or committed. Tests assert both original panic messages locally, typed failure
counts, continued indexing, and physical page locators for surviving pages.

## Ranking goldens (RRF k=5)

`counts-rrf-k5.json` and `ready-rrf-k5.json` freeze the complete synthetic
ranking results after the intentional default fusion change from RRF k=60 to
k=5. The original captures came from main `28814a85` (counts) and `71f9a18`
(ready search). They were refreshed from the new engine on a branch based on
main `dc649344`, using Rust 1.99.0 and `FakeEmbedder`.

Only temporary paths, source mtimes and elapsed milliseconds are normalized.
Scores, ordering, signals, locators, hashes, previews and deterministic stats
remain covered. The ready fixture still excludes the later additive `match`
field; the counts fixture covers it in full. These are regression snapshots
for the new default, not a claim that rankings remain identical to old main.
The focused `hybrid_rrf_k5_preserves_a_strong_semantic_lead` test independently
pins the fusion behavior.

`match-ranking-rrf-k5.jsonl` and `match-pdf-rrf-k5.jsonl` extend the same
coverage to 168 text and 144 mixed text/PDF cases across memory and SQLite
caches. Originally captured on main `71f9a184`, they were regenerated from
the k=5 engine after integrating main through `7c4012ed`. They retain all
case settings, hit order, query identities and signal/locator fields. Only
normalized fusion score bits change: 196 hybrid and 68 lexical scores.
Semantic cases remain byte-identical. An independent float32 calculation
from the frozen semantic, keyword and filename ranks reproduced both the
old k=60 snapshots and the new k=5 captures exactly across all 312 cases.
Lexical mode also uses RRF normalization, so its scores change even when
its ordering does not. The complete snapshot assertions remain in place.

To intentionally refresh a golden, temporarily replace the test's final
assertion with a write of `actual`, run that integration test, then restore the
assertion and rerun it against the captured fixture. Review the resulting diff:
only intended ranking changes belong in a refresh. Never refresh these fixtures
to silence an unexplained failure.
